stories.Headline: Amgen to open New Science & Innovation Center in Genome Valley, Hyderabad
stories.Summary:
Amgen announced plans to establish a new Science and Innovation Center in Hyderabad's Genome Valley region, which will become part of the company's seven-laboratory global research network. The facility is expected to open in 2027 and will integrate advanced scientific capabilities with digital innovation to accelerate medicine discovery and development. Scientists and technologists will work across discovery chemistry, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics, and precision medicine at the center.

This expansion reflects Amgen's commitment to leveraging India's strong life sciences ecosystem and demonstrates Hyderabad's growing importance as a global research hub. The new center will work closely with Amgen's existing technology and innovation site in the same city, combining wet-laboratory science with advanced technology. Officials highlighted how this investment represents a significant step in establishing Hyderabad as a center for discovering and developing next-generation medicines for global patients.

stories.Headline: Government of Kerala Partners with SAS to Strengthen Social Welfare Schemes Delivery using Artificial Intelligence
stories.Summary:
The Government of Kerala has partnered with SAS, a global data and artificial intelligence company, to improve how social welfare programs are delivered across the state. Kerala State IT Mission selected SAS as a strategic analytics partner to strengthen governance and service delivery through advanced data analytics capabilities. The collaboration aims to streamline beneficiary management for all social protection schemes by detecting duplicate citizen records, enhancing real-time decision-making, improving compliance monitoring, and strengthening the efficiency of welfare scheme delivery.

Through this initiative, Kerala intends to consolidate data across departments to boost transparency and accountability in social welfare programs. The partnership aligns with Kerala's broader vision to use technology for inclusive growth and transparent governance. According to officials, the state aims to set a strong example for data-driven governance in India by leveraging SAS's analytics capabilities to turn complex data into meaningful insights that support better governance outcomes and citizen-focused innovation.

stories.Headline: IFSCA Grants Nexent Capital GIFT City Investment Banking License
stories.Summary:
Nexent Capital, the Indian subsidiary of a U.S. investment firm, has received approval from India's International Financial Services Centre Authority to operate as an investment banker in GIFT City. The registration was granted on July 31, 2026, and allows the company to manage initial public offerings, follow-on offerings, SPAC listings, and other capital market activities within the regulatory framework of India's financial center.

The firm plans to use this license to help international companies, particularly from the United States and Europe, raise capital and list their shares through GIFT City's exchanges. Nexent Capital currently has potential clients in technology sectors including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data centers, and quantum computing. The company aims to provide comprehensive advisory services throughout the entire process, from initial structuring through post-listing support.

stories.Headline: NACDC 2026 Concludes at UBC, Advancing Global AI & Technology Research
stories.Summary:
The North American Conference on Computational Intelligence, Data Science and Cloud Computing concluded on August 12, 2026, at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver after a three-day event. The conference was organized by the Institute of Engineering and Management in Kolkata, India, in partnership with the University of Engineering and Management Kolkata, Nova Publishers, and Smart Society Canada. The event brought together academics, scientists, researchers, and industry professionals to discuss developments in computational intelligence, data science, and cloud computing, featuring keynote lectures, paper presentations, workshops, and awards ceremonies.

The conference attracted over 12,000 participants from more than 35 countries, including the United States, Canada, Australia, Malaysia, Egypt, and South Africa. Research papers were selected through a rigorous peer-review process with an acceptance rate of approximately 26 percent. Four dedicated tracks organized the technical presentations covering computational intelligence and artificial intelligence, data science and big data analytics, cloud computing and infrastructure, and advanced emerging technologies. The conference proceedings will be published by Nova Science Publishers.

stories.Headline: PSU Major DFCCIL Awards Letter of Acceptance to Magellanic Cloud Limited Subsidiary, Deepening Pan-India PSU Portfolio
stories.Summary:
Magellanic Cloud Limited announced that its subsidiary, Provigil Surveillance Limited, received a contract worth 3.73 crore rupees from India's Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation. The five-year contract involves supplying, installing, and maintaining an electronic surveillance system along a section of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor. The system will handle theft prevention, remote monitoring, asset protection, and perimeter security across the specified railway section using an operations-based model.

The contract strengthens Provigil's position in India's public sector infrastructure projects and demonstrates growing confidence from major government agencies in the company's surveillance and security capabilities. The project is expected to add to Magellanic Cloud's order book and expand its footprint in the surveillance and security solutions segment. The company, headquartered in Hyderabad, serves over 100 clients across multiple countries and specializes in digital transformation, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and surveillance technologies.

stories.Headline: Artmarket.com: Q2 2026 Upward Trend, from Progressive Transition to Artprice's "AI-FIRST" Metamorphosis
stories.Summary:
Artmarket.com announced strong second quarter 2026 performance and revealed a major strategic shift in its artificial intelligence integration. Founder Thierry Ehrmann and the controlling Groupe Serveur family plan to increase their shareholdings in the company, demonstrating confidence in its growth trajectory. The company is accelerating its transformation from a gradual AI rollout to a comprehensive "AI-First" architecture centered on its proprietary databases and two main AI systems called Intuitive Art Market and Blind Spot.

Rather than incrementally adding AI features to existing systems, Artprice is overhauling its entire operational infrastructure internally before releasing it to subscribers. The company emphasized that controlling its own data pipelines and algorithms gives it a competitive advantage in an era where much internet content contains unreliable synthetic data. The complete platform will eventually offer subscribers autonomous AI agents for market analysis, forecasting, and risk modeling through subscription fees ranging from 1,600 to 2,500 dollars annually. This transformation represents a fundamental change in how Artprice operates, evolving from a historical database into an active decision-making system.

stories.Headline: Punjab National Bank (PNB) to Deploy Magellanic Cloud's E-Surveillance Solutions Across 1,000 ATMs Nationwide
stories.Summary:
Magellanic Cloud Limited's subsidiary, IVIS International Private Limited, has secured multiple purchase orders from NCR Corporation India Private Limited to install surveillance solutions across 1,000 Punjab National Bank ATM locations nationwide. The contract is valued at approximately 18.4 crore rupees and spans five years, encompassing both capital expenditure and operational expenditure components. This deployment demonstrates IVIS's capability to execute large-scale surveillance projects across distributed banking networks.

The company, headquartered in Hyderabad, specializes in digital transformation and artificial intelligence-driven surveillance systems. According to Magellanic Cloud's Chairman and Managing Director Joseph Sudheer Reddy Thumma, the banking and financial services sector has been a strategic focus for over 15 years. The order reinforces the company's position in delivering technology-enabled security solutions for critical financial infrastructure and reflects its ability to address the growing security needs of major Indian banks. The company employs over 1,600 professionals and serves more than 100 clients across multiple countries.

stories.Headline: The Excellence List 2026 | 10 Extraordinary Personalities
stories.Summary:
The Excellence List 2026 highlights ten accomplished individuals making significant contributions across India. The list includes Sundeep Kochar, a celebrity astrologer and life coach with 26 years of experience who gained recognition through the television show Kismat Ke Sitare, and Pt. Umesh Chandra Pant, a distinguished Vedic astrologer who founded PavitraJyotish and has received multiple professional honors. Advocate Sarthak Chaturvedi serves as Senior Panel Counsel for the Government of India at the Supreme Court and chairs the Anti-Doping Disciplinary Panel. Dr. M. Hussain Kalsekar is an entrepreneur with 19 years of experience who leads 366 DigitX, a digital solutions company, and has received recognition including a Forbes 200 India nomination in 2024.

The remaining honorees include Punam Gupta, founder of Together We Can Foundation, an NGO focused on food safety and social causes, and Neha Singh, CEO of Securium Solutions, a cybersecurity company that has completed over 2,500 projects and trained 2 million students. Parvaan Vohra, age 25, founded two fashion brands including Sick My Duck Clothing known for bold streetwear. Sambhav Karnawat, an IIT graduate and fourth-generation jeweler, founded Jewelove, specializing in pure platinum jewelry. Additional honorees include professionals in healthcare, entrepreneurship, and global marketing sectors.

stories.Headline: Parliamentary panel rejects govt response on cyber fraud, says it fails to plug key gaps
stories.Summary:
A Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance in India has rejected the government's response to cyber fraud prevention, concluding that proposed measures are primarily procedural and fail to address significant operational weaknesses. The committee criticized the Department of Financial Services for not adequately tackling the problem of fraudulent funds being transferred through mule accounts, which are bank accounts used to receive and quickly move stolen money.

The panel raised several specific concerns about the government's approach, including insufficient accountability for banks that host mule accounts and failure to address the critical three to four hour window after fraud occurs when funds can potentially be recovered. Under the proposed compensation framework, banks would only bear ten percent of losses while the central bank assumes sixty five percent, creating inadequate incentive for banks to prevent fraud. The committee recommended establishing a penal framework that would penalize banks for KYC verification failures and hold them accountable when they host multiple mule accounts.

stories.Headline: Supreme Court Declines Plea Seeking Regulation Of AI Use By Central And State Governments; Asks Centre To Consider Representation
stories.Summary:
The Supreme Court rejected a plea requesting judicial guidelines to regulate artificial intelligence use by the Union and State Governments. The petitioner, NK Goswami, sought constitutional safeguards for high-risk AI systems used in welfare distribution, policing, surveillance, and content moderation. He asked the court to mandate human oversight, algorithmic impact assessments, bias audits, and transparency requirements. A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant declined to intervene, stating the issue falls within the policy domain rather than the judiciary's scope, and noting the court lacks technical expertise in this area.

The court instructed the Centre to consider a representation the petitioner had previously submitted in February addressing these concerns. The judges acknowledged that AI use within the judicial system is already well-regulated through comprehensive guidelines. The court permitted the petitioner to supplement his representation by sending a copy of the petition to relevant authorities, allowing the government to take appropriate measures if it chooses to do so.
